recipes.name: Cornell Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 to 3 1/2 pound) broiler-fryer chicken, cut in half

steps.text: Purée cider vinegar, oil, egg, salt, poultry seasoning, and pepper in a blender until smooth.
Pour marinade into a resealable plastic bag. Add chicken halves, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove chicken halves from the bag and transfer to a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Pat chicken dry with more paper towels. Reserve marinade.

Place chicken, skin-side down, onto the preheated grill over direct heat. Grill for 2 minutes, then turn each piece, brush with marinade, and move to indirect heat. Continue to cook, turning often and brushing with marinade, until nicely browned and meat is no longer pink in the center, about 45 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone, should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Let rest for 5 to 10 minutes before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Cornell Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Dr. Baker's Cornell chicken recipe remains a favorite after more than 50 years. An easy seasoned apple cider marinade keeps it moist and flavorful.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful. Except, instead of reserving the used/contaminated marinade to periodically baste with, reserve about 3/4 cup prior to marinating the chicken. Now you have a nice fresh uncontaminated sauce to baste with.

My father made this chicken on the grill all the time and since I hated the smell of vinegar, he wouldn't tell me what was in it. This is the BEST chicken ever! I make it myself now. I do decrease the salt by half, but that's it. Make sure you've got a lot of chicken, this goes a long way. Also, I have boiled the chicken in the marinade ahead of time for about 15 minutes then transferred to the grill so it has the flavor really deeply infused and the meat is done on the grill without burning it. Again, BEST CHICKEN EVER!

I made it a couple of weeks ago using 3.5 lbs of chicken thighs. I used only 1 cup of ACV and cut the amount of salt down to 1 tbsp. I vacuum sealed the contents for 24 hours and cooked it according to the directions. Incredible!

This is SO good- I remember having this marinade on chicken growing up- or something close to it- the only difference was to use melted butter instead of the oil and no egg. I do this recipe as written- although I had no poultry seasoning, so added some garlic instead- I also used on boneless skinless chicken breast- AWESOME! Tender and flavorful! Best on a charcoal grill. 2nd review- WONDERFUL! After I take the chicken out of the marinade (overnight) I boil the used marinade for 10 minutes to 'de-contaminate' it then use that boiled marinade to dip the chicken pieces in as I am grilling it, approximately every 10-15 minutes- every time I turn the chicken.

The marinade smelled awful to me, but I used it anyway, reserving some for basting later. I only added 2 Tbls. salt because my poultry seasoning had salt in it too. At first bite I wondered why this chicken had such high ratings, but the more I ate the better it got. I grilled it over charcoal and the skin was crispy and the meat was nice and juicy! The flavor turned out surprisingly pleasant.
I've been making this recipe for over 50 years. Good every time. Not necessary to use a blender, just put ingredients in a jar and shake well. Once less tool to clean!

This was a very good grilled chicken, not the best I've ever had but decidedly good. I only marinated for a day (not overnight as I normally would) due to reviews of this technically being a basting sauce not a marinade. I think it could have marinated longer and been fine. I was cooking for kids so I did 1 1/2 cups cider vinegar and 1/2 cup apple juice. I indirectly grilled then put them over the flames to crisp them up at the end. I also used immersion basting several times (after I heated/thickened the marinade in a saucepan on the stove) which worked nicely, and kept the grill from getting too messy! Would make again.
I will air fry it , mine broils at 550. Lets see. Cut salt amount in half. Looking good so far.

Excellent recipe! I prepared this using Split Chicken cuts (leg w/ attached thigh) and cooked using the Sous Vide water bath method at 158 Deg F for 3.5 hours. Finish on a charcoal or pellet grill to a barbeque glaze.

This turned out really well. I let the chicken marinate ( a little was reserved for basting) overnight, but sadly, due to the weather I had to use the oven. I hit the broiler the last few minutes trying for a bit of color....seemed to work well enough. It was tender and juicy, every time I opened the oven door to baste them, my eyes would burn a little from the vinegar but no one found it overwhelming while eating. I can't wait to try again using the grill!

We use this recipe weekly to have grilled chicken at the ready for salads and sandwiches. It's excellent! We often use breasts and not whole chicken. We once left it marinating for two days and it was still great.
This has great flavor, and my 5yo says it's his favorite kind of chicken - worth trying!
I wonder if this is close to Mr. Chicken I loved so much in Watkins Glen NY, RIP Mr. Chicken, you were the best!

Easy peasy! I grew up in Upstate NY, so had this chicken often. I also save out part of the marinade for basting. This can be jazzed up.with more seasonings if you like, but this basic recipe is a winner winner chicken dinner!

Very popular here in central New York, it's known simply as "chicken bbq." Big fundraisers, they always sell out quickly. I marinate for a day or two, cook in a pressure cooker, and then put on the grill or under the broiler to crisp up the skin.

I followed directions as indicated. Chicken tasted like simple grilled chicken. There was little tang and little flavor. With all due respect to the good professor, I will stick to my homemade Kansas City style.

Grew up eating this chicken in western NY. Still my favorite grilled chicken recipe. Cook the reserved marinade to prevent cross contamination. We pull the chicken when the leg bone can be easily turned and place it in a cooler to stay warm. Douse the chicken with marinade when putting it in the cooler for extra tang.

When I was a kid growing up in Upstate New York the fire department used this Cornell chicken to raise money. I live in North Carolina now and make it for my kids and neighbors, and they Love it!!! I make it once a month, and I never have leftovers.
Firehouse chicken is great my dad used to make it quite a bit when I was a kid and he passed away and I carried the recipe on
I made this two days after making "Barbecued Butter Chicken". I smoked it at 325 and used white pepper instead of black. So delicious. We'll be making this again too. Thanks Chef John.
